title: Local eventual image freeness and finite quotient charts
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite normed Q_ℓ-extension, X a scheme with noetherian underlying space, and P a locally finitely presented module over R_X, the continuous integral coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. There exists a pro-etale cover C of X such that on each member C_s there is a bound N_s with the following property for every n≥N_s: the pullback of image(ℓ^n id_P) is finite free over the pulled-back integral coefficient ring, and the pullback of the underlying set sheaf of cokernel(ℓ^n id_P) is isomorphic to the constant sheaf on some finite set. The bound may vary with s; this theorem makes no global choice of exponent and constructs no epimorphism or resolution.

proof.text: Extend P to rational coefficients and apply field local triviality (resolutionRationalLF). On a local finite-presentation cover, normalize the pulled-back integral coefficient ring using its canonical isomorphism. The rational cokernel of the resulting finite matrix is locally finite free. Prove local scalar charts for this matrix by strong induction on the number of source generators.

Apply integralMatrix_analytic_cover to obtain zero-matrix pieces or a nowhere-zero entry dominating every matrix entry in norm. The zero matrix has a finite-free cokernel. In the nonzero case, integralMatrix_entry_properties gives row division and rational invertibility of the pivot; integralMatrix_column_divides proves column division using continuous integral division. The finitePivotSplit basis isomorphisms give the explicit two-sided block matrix (finiteBiproduct_double_pivot).

Elementary block elimination (integralPivotCokernelIso) identifies the matrix cokernel with the binary direct sum of its pivot cokernel and its Schur-complement cokernel. Rational invertibility of the pivot and mappedPivotCokernelIso show that the latter cokernel remains rationally locally finite free. Its source rank is strictly smaller, so the induction hypothesis supplies its local scalar charts. A simultaneous global diagonal form is not needed.

For the cyclic pivot, refine by open neighborhoods on which its nonzero norm is constant. integralRegularCoefficient_pullback identifies the restricted pivot function. The proved principal-quotient comparisons identify its cokernel with a constant finite set, and integralConstantNormCokernelBound gives an eventual annihilating power of ℓ. Thus its eventual scalar image is zero and finite free. For a finite-free module, scalar multiplication by ℓ^n is monic, its image is finite free, and integralFiniteFreeQuotientSetConstant gives a finite constant quotient for every exponent.

Combine the two scalar charts on a common pro-etale refinement using the maximum of their bounds (localScalarCharts_biprod). Images and cokernels of scalar maps respect module isomorphisms, coefficient-ring isomorphisms, and composition of pullbacks. Bind the covers through the induction and the initial finite presentations. Finally, exact pullback preserves images and cokernels, and chartSetPullbackIso identifies the underlying set of the abelian pullback with the actual set-sheaf inverse image in the statement. The latter comparison uses the terminal object in each left Kan extension indexing category, so forgetting abelian groups preserves the colimits in question. This proves the original statement, including zero ranks and empty cover members.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_lfp_local_torsion_charts
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : Type) [NormedField E]
    [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (CondensedRing.integralCoeff ℓ E) X))
    (hP : IsLocallyFinitelyPresented
      (condensedRingObj (CondensedRing.integralCoeff ℓ E) X) P) :
    ∃ C : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ s : C.I₀,
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        Mod.IsFree ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (C.f s)).obj
          (condensedRingObj (CondensedRing.integralCoeff ℓ E) X))
          (((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (C.f s)).mapMod _).obj
            (image ((ℓ ^ n) • 𝟙 P))) ∧
        ∃ k : ℕ, Nonempty
          ((Scheme.proEtaleSheafInverseImage (C.f s) (Type (u + 1))).obj
            ((Mod.forget _ ⋙ sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
              (forget Ab.{u + 1})).obj (cokernel ((ℓ ^ n) • 𝟙 P))) ≅
            (constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (C.X s)) (Type (u + 1))).obj
              (ULift.{u + 1} (Fin k)))
